initial.ariaLabel: Expression graph. 1 of 5 nodes visible; a=2

whilePlaying.caption: Start with a = 2. A Value holds one number (data) and one gradient (grad), which is still zero.
whilePlaying.ariaLabel: Expression graph. 1 of 5 nodes visible; a=2

afterPlay.caption: Add b = -3. Inputs are plain Values; no operation connects them yet.
afterPlay.ariaLabel: Expression graph. 2 of 5 nodes visible; a=2, b=-3

afterPause.caption: Add b = -3. Inputs are plain Values; no operation connects them yet.
afterPause.ariaLabel: Expression graph. 2 of 5 nodes visible; a=2, b=-3

mid.caption: Add the third input: c = 10.
mid.ariaLabel: Expression graph. 4 of 5 nodes visible; a=2, b=-3, mul=-6, c=10

final.caption: Backward pass: d.grad = 1. Then mul.grad = 1 and c.grad = 1; the chain rule gives a.grad = b = -3 and b.grad = a = 2.
final.ariaLabel: Expression graph. 5 of 5 nodes visible; a=2 (grad -3), b=-3 (grad 2), mul=-6 (grad 1), c=10 (grad 1), add=4 (grad 1)

entry.caption: We already have d = a × b + c = 4. Backward starts at the output and walks the graph in reverse topological order, accumulating each node’s grad.
entry.ariaLabel: Expression graph. 5 of 5 nodes visible; a=2, b=-3, mul=-6, c=10, add=4

playing.caption: We already have d = a × b + c = 4. Backward starts at the output and walks the graph in reverse topological order, accumulating each node’s grad.
playing.ariaLabel: Expression graph. 5 of 5 nodes visible; a=2, b=-3, mul=-6, c=10, add=4

topo.caption: Only operations are numbered: ① + must run before ② ×. The × node’s gradient has to be complete before it can pass anything back to a and b — that is the reverse topological order.
topo.ariaLabel: Expression graph. 5 of 5 nodes visible; a=2, b=-3, mul=-6, c=10, add=4

seed.caption: Seed the output: d.grad = 1 (∂d/∂d). Every other grad is still zero.
seed.ariaLabel: Expression graph. 5 of 5 nodes visible; a=2, b=-3, mul=-6, c=10, add=4 (grad 1)

throughAdd.caption: Process ① +: d.grad = 1 flows back along both edges. The local derivatives are ∂d/∂mul = 1 and ∂d/∂c = 1, so mul.grad = 1 and c.grad = 1.
throughAdd.ariaLabel: Expression graph. 5 of 5 nodes visible; a=2, b=-3, mul=-6 (grad 1), c=10 (grad 1), add=4 (grad 1)

throughMul.caption: Process ② ×: mul.grad = 1 flows to a and b. The local derivatives are ∂mul/∂a = b = -3 and ∂mul/∂b = a = 2, so a.grad = 1 × -3 = -3 and b.grad = 1 × 2 = 2.
throughMul.ariaLabel: Expression graph. 5 of 5 nodes visible; a=2 (grad -3), b=-3 (grad 2), mul=-6 (grad 1), c=10 (grad 1), add=4 (grad 1)

final.caption: Done. Chain rule along a → mul → d: ∂d/∂a = ∂d/∂mul · ∂mul/∂a = 1 · b = -3. Reverse topological order made mul.grad complete before it was used.
final.ariaLabel: Expression graph. 5 of 5 nodes visible; a=2 (grad -3), b=-3 (grad 2), mul=-6 (grad 1), c=10 (grad 1), add=4 (grad 1)

throughW1.caption: Process ×: p1.grad flows into w1 and x1. ∂p1/∂w1 = x1 = 1, so w1.grad = 1 × 0.79 = 0.79; ∂p1/∂x1 = w1 = 0.5, so x1.grad = 0.79.
